accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:armwise-discordance-budget and all headline results
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The latent armwise discordance bound s is analyst-selected and is not identifiable from pretreatment records or observed outcomes.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All minimax risks, optimizer faces, asymptotic claims, and confidence sets are conditional on the selected s or sequence (s_J), with sensitivity reporting across values rather than data-driven selection of s.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and Section 2 discussion of Theorem 2.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The result makes uniform randomization over the permutation orbit minimax for a given assignment vector and invariant estimator; its subsequent optimal-estimation result is restricted to further assumptions and linear estimators.
The paper studies minimax precision for a two-arm experiment with conditional means in a given set and shows structured cases can require randomization beyond a single partition.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1, 5--7, and 21; abstract, equations (4) and (10), proof of Theorem 2.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The unrestricted binary all-design/all-estimator problem reduces to an experiment with scalar observation and two unknown parameters, has an Airy second-order expansion, and is attained by balanced Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3 and 8; discussion of estimator class and Theorem 1/equation (4)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 optimizes over all measurable estimators and gives the unrestricted bounded-potential-outcome minimax value; the paper identifies independent assignment as optimal.
The paper establishes a matched-pair design as maximally precise among stratified schemes treating units with probability one half, with a baseline-outcome special case.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(548), 2024, pp. 2934--2946
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The Gram--Schmidt Walk paper formalizes a covariate-balance/robustness tradeoff for Horvitz--Thompson estimation and provides finite-sample MSE guarantees plus asymptotic inference conditions.
The result is for design-unbiased estimation of bounded finite-population totals and identifies pairwise-independent inclusion indicators as sharp for that restricted decision class.
Under within-pair coin flips, the paper finds a single boundary-corner worst compatible pattern and obtains an O(log S) binary-tail inversion procedure.
The paper gives finite-sample exact binary ATE intervals with O(log n) randomization tests for balanced Bernoulli and matched-pair designs, and O(n^2) for general Bernoulli designs.

The paper extends exact/conservative binary ATE inference to stratified experiments by permutation-test inversion over compatible potential-outcome tables, with potentially product-form computational burden.
